note: Shared behavioral scenario fixtures for programs/pinocchio-vault, per docs/vault-design.md. This is the single source of truth for WHICH scenarios the Rust and JS/TS test suites must both cover, so scenario coverage cannot silently drift between the two language test suites. Exact instruction bytes/account pubkeys are not encoded here (PDAs and fresh keypairs are inherently per-test-run values in this program); each scenario instead names the setup and the expected outcome, and each language's test harness constructs the concrete instruction/accounts from that.
implementationStatus: `Initialize`, `Deposit`, and `Withdraw` are all implemented. `Initialize` covers 1 happy path + 9 rejections. `Deposit`/`Withdraw` scenarios cover every checklist item applicable to each instruction (docs/security-checklist.md) plus boundary cases. Extension-rejection scenarios remain Initialize-only, since mint extension enforcement (§7) happens only there.

scenarios.name: happy_path_initialize
scenarios.description: Owner initializes a vault over an extension-free Token-2022 mint. Vault state PDA and program-derived token account are both created; token account authority is the vault state PDA, never the owner.

scenarios.name: rejects_wrong_account_count
scenarios.description: Fewer or more than the 6 required accounts are supplied.

scenarios.name: rejects_duplicate_accounts
scenarios.description: Two account slots that must differ (e.g. vault_state and vault_token_account) hold the same pubkey.

scenarios.name: rejects_double_initialize
scenarios.description: Initialize is called again on a vault_state account whose account_init_flag is already 1. Checked FIRST, before any other logic (docs/vault-design.md §8 step 3), so this must fire even if every other input in the second call is otherwise valid.
scenarios.setup: vault_state pre-initialized by a prior successful Initialize

scenarios.name: rejects_missing_signer
scenarios.description: owner account is not marked as a transaction signer.

scenarios.name: rejects_invalid_instruction_tag
scenarios.description: First byte of instruction data is not 0 (the only tag Initialize's build accepts today -- 1/2 are reserved for Deposit/Withdraw and not yet wired).

scenarios.name: rejects_deserialization_error
scenarios.description: Instruction tag is valid (0) but trailing bytes follow it -- Initialize takes no arguments, so any extra data is malformed. Distinct from an invalid tag: this proves the tag check runs BEFORE this check, not that this check doesn't exist.

scenarios.name: rejects_mint_not_owned_by_token_2022
scenarios.description: mint account's owner is not the Token-2022 program (e.g. a legacy SPL Token mint, or an arbitrary account).

scenarios.name: rejects_unsupported_mint_extension
scenarios.description: mint carries any initialized Token-2022 extension TLV entry. docs/vault-design.md §7's accepted-extension set is empty in v1 (default-reject posture), enforced today as one blanket rule in token2022.rs rather than 6 separate per-extension checks -- this is one representative scenario, not 6; the per-extension test names in docs/security-checklist.md are Step 6 work once per-extension handling (if any) is actually implemented, not before.
scenarios.setup: mint has >=1 initialized TLV extension entry (any type)

scenarios.name: rejects_forged_token_program
scenarios.description: token_program account passed is not the hardcoded Token-2022 program ID.

scenarios.name: rejects_forged_system_program
scenarios.description: system_program account passed is not the real System Program.

scenarios.name: happy_path_deposit
scenarios.description: Any signer (not necessarily vault.owner -- deposits are permissionless top-ups) transfers amount from their own token account into the vault's program-derived token account.
scenarios.setup: default, depositor != vault owner, depositor_token_account funded with >= amount

scenarios.name: rejects_wrong_state_owner
scenarios.description: vault_state account is not owned by this program (e.g. a System-owned or arbitrary account substituted in).

scenarios.name: rejects_deserialization_error
scenarios.description: Tag is valid (1) but the remaining bytes are not exactly 8 (a well-formed little-endian u64). Distinct from an invalid tag: proves the tag check runs before this one.

scenarios.name: rejects_substituted_token_account
scenarios.description: vault_token_account supplied does not equal the address re-derived from vault_state (Decision 4) -- e.g. a real Token-2022 account for the same mint but the wrong PDA.

scenarios.name: rejects_forged_cpi_target
scenarios.description: token_program account passed is not the hardcoded Token-2022 program ID.

scenarios.name: boundary_zero_amount_deposit
scenarios.description: amount == 0 is a valid (no-op-value) transfer_checked call; Token-2022 accepts it and it must not be rejected by the vault program itself.

scenarios.name: happy_path_withdraw
scenarios.description: vault.owner withdraws amount <= the vault token account's real balance; CPI is invoke_signed by the vault state PDA using the stored bump, never the owner's own signature.

scenarios.name: rejects_non_owner_withdraw
scenarios.description: A signer who is not vault.owner attempts Withdraw. Pre-mortem #1 -- the primary drain-the-vault attack this template exists to demonstrate defeating.

scenarios.name: rejects_forged_bump
scenarios.description: vault_state supplied does not re-derive from [b"vault", owner_pubkey] + vault.bump -- simulates an attacker-influenced or stale account substituted for the real vault state PDA. The program only ever uses the *stored* bump for invoke_signed, never one from instruction data, so there is no separate 'forged instruction-data bump' path to test (pre-mortem #2, closed by construction).

scenarios.name: rejects_overdraw
scenarios.description: amount > vault_token_account.amount (the token account's real on-chain balance, the single source of truth -- not a duplicated ledger in VaultState).

scenarios.name: boundary_max_u64_overdraw
scenarios.description: amount = u64::MAX against a vault token account with a small real balance -- must fail as an ordinary overdraw, not panic/overflow (checked comparison, not checked_sub on the requested amount itself).
